identity.title: [v0.92][C-SDLC][297.c][test] Prove projection recovery crash, topology, race, and idempotency behavior

review_prompts: Are both prerequisite terminal and ancestry gates exact and fail closed before bind?
Does every production mutation and durability boundary have before/after restart proof?
Can any mock, constant, path, or self-authored receipt become authority?
Are symlink, repeated-inode, ancestor-swap, destination-race, recovery/cleanup, ordinary-commit, and sentinel cases explicit?
Does scope remain one new integration test target plus issue-local records?

findings.summary: The cleanup half of #300 is not fed by production-generated recovery authority; it currently constructs a synthetic terminal envelope, completed recovery receipt, and archive manifest instead of consuming a real recovery-to-cleanup bridge.
findings.route: #297 parent integration must provide or explicitly route the production recovery-to-cleanup authority bridge before #300 can pass.

findings.summary: The #300 integration target does not itself enumerate or mechanically prove the approved before/after recovery and cleanup failpoint matrix, conflicting-operation rejection, or full adversarial filesystem/request matrix; gate5 evidence cannot be overclaimed unless #300 mechanically invokes/proves those cases.
findings.route: Either make the #300 integration target mechanically invoke/prove the existing deep matrix cases or enumerate the missing integration cases explicitly before fresh review.
